title: Two computers for molecular chemistry: where could quantum advantage come from?
summary: Quantum and classical computers can take on different parts of a molecular energy calculation. A Qunova nitrogen benchmark records 4 minutes 18 seconds of QPU use and nearly 13 hours overall, putting both the results and the costs of this division of work in view. Following quantum proposals of electronic configurations and classical solutions of the wavefunction, this review examines what it would take to reach the same accuracy at a lower total cost.
